_: The Seventh Course, Friday's case (Jay, 2026-10-22: the whole dinner scripted and spoken, the diners act it; 2026-10-24: a plain murder mystery, not dinner theatre, and no lulls). Source of services/hubs/src/lounge/mysteries/fri.json (mystery-script.py).
title: THE SEVENTH COURSE: WHO KILLED MAX HARROW?

spring.text: His Arnhem was in spring. It was September

vial.text: A vial of digitalis gone from Nancy's bag

novel.text: Edith's new book: cyanide in a toast

notebook.text: Max's notebook: R.A. was never at Arnhem

lines: Ten years in this flat, Celia. And the view still costs more than the furniture.
Nor does it read my column. Which is more than I can say for anyone here.
I read it every Monday, Max. In the bath. It's the only place I can bear it.
Missus Vane, you say the loveliest things.
Uncle Rupert, there are two empty chairs at the table. Who else is coming?
Our two friends from the lounge, Nancy. They sit in the middle. They hear everything.
Then they had better keep their ears open. Things get said at dinners.
Things get said. And on Monday, things get printed.
Not tonight, Max. Tonight is our anniversary.
Ten years. I gave it two. I lost a pound to Hobbs on it.
Then let's go in before Hobbs wants another pound. Celia, your arm.
Nancy, darling, you look exhausted. Have they had you on nights again?
Four in a row. I could sleep standing up. Don't let me near the claret.
Inspector, mind the step. You always miss the step.
Thirty years at the Yard, Missus Vane. I have never once missed a step.
You missed one at my christening. Mother still talks about it.
I'm by the window, I see. The best seat for watching everybody.
You always take the best seat, Max. Even when it isn't yours.
Thank you for having me, Rupert. Celia says you've been planning a surprise all week.
Not planning, Locke. Choosing. There's a difference, as you'll see at the sorbet.
Glasses up, everyone. To Celia. Ten years, and she has not poisoned me once.
And now, for our two friends in the middle, some introductions.
My wife, Lady Celia. She married me for the view.
My niece, Nancy. A nurse at Saint Thomas's. She keeps us all alive.
Most of you. On a good night.
Missus Edith Vane. She lives downstairs and murders people for a living.
On paper, Rupert. Only on paper. It pays better than the real thing.
Inspector Locke. Scotland Yard, retired. Celia's godfather.
I used to arrest people. Now I mostly arrest greenfly.
And Max Harrow, who writes The Harrow Report. Every Monday, half of London wakes up ruined.
And Hobbs, our butler. Hobbs knows where all the bodies are buried.
Only the ones in the cellar, my lord.
Rupert, are you speaking at the regiment dinner in November?
I always speak, Max. They ask for the bridge every year.
We had wasps at Ashcombe this summer. Dreadful. A nest in every chimney.
I had Jenkins put the cyanide down in August. Not a wasp left in the county.
Cyanide! How marvellous. Where does one buy cyanide?
The chemist in the village. You sign a little book.
I must remember that. For work.
Please don't remember it at the table.
Edith, how is the new book? Who dies this time?
A sea captain. It's called Death at the Captain's Table. It's out in March.
I never tell, Max. Not even my publisher knows. Well. Rupert knows. He read the proofs.
I said the ending was too obvious.
You say that about everything, Rupert. You said it about the moon landing.
Uncle Rupert, are you taking your drops? Every night?
Every night, Nurse. One drop, in water. I'm a model patient.
Don't, Nancy. Our friends don't want to hear about the war over the salmon.
Oh, they do. Go on, Rupert. The bridge.
Well. If you insist. Spring of forty four. The blossom was out on the trees. I remember that. The blossom, and the noise.
We held that bridge for three days. Three days, and no tea.
Was it? Well. It felt like spring. One was young.
I'm eating, darling. I'm just savouring Rupert's war. It's the best thing on the menu.
Inspector, were you ever in the army?
The Military Police, Missus Vane. Nineteen fifty three. I arrested a great many heroes.
Max, what's in Monday's column? You've been grinning like a cat all evening.
Monday. Monday, The Harrow Report will tell London about a war hero who was never at the war.
A chest full of medals, bought at an auction in Brighton. Three pounds, the lot.
Somebody very well known. Somebody who dines out on it. Every night of the week.
That's half the men at my club.
Max, that's cruel. Those men were proud of something.
Proud of something they didn't do, darling. That's what makes it a story.
Not by this one, Rupert. This one wouldn't dare stand up in a court.
A drop, Hobbs. A big drop.
Inspector, do you miss it? The Yard?
I miss the poisoners, Nancy. They were the only clever ones.
He solved the Brixton poisonings. The vicar.
Every poisoner I ever caught had one habit, Celia. They always insisted on pouring.
Then I must be a terrible suspect, Locke. I pour everything in this house.
He does. Ten years, and Hobbs has never once poured the good stuff.
I am permitted the sherry, my lady. On Tuesdays.
Tell them about the vicar, Inspector. It was in the communion wine, wasn't it?
In the flask he carried for the sick. He visited eleven parishioners. Six of them left him money.
It was very efficient, Nancy. Murder usually is. It's getting away with it that takes imagination.
Max, the soup is coming. Behave.
The soup is served, my lord.
Celia, you're wearing the green. I always liked you in the green.
Max, you're very attentive to Celia tonight.
I'm attentive to everyone, Edith. It's my job.
Your job is selling other people's secrets, Max.
How are things at the hospital, Nancy?
Busy. I'm on call tonight, so if anyone collapses, aim for me.
Nancy carries a whole pharmacy in that bag of hers.
Somebody has to. Uncle Rupert's heart pills, Aunt Celia's sleeping pills, Edith's everything pills.
Oh, my bag. I left it out on the terrace. Excuse me, I'm on call.
Rupert, the soup is excellent. Is it the same cook?
The same cook for twenty years. She hates you, Max.
Everybody's cook hates me. I write about their dinners.
You wrote that my fish pie tasted of regret.
It did, Edith. It tasted of years of it.
Celia, the flowers are lovely. From the country?
From the florist on the corner, Inspector. The country only grows wasps.
And Jenkins. Who is mostly a wasp.
Sorry. All quiet at the hospital. Nobody's dying yet.
Nancy, are you still set on Canada?
Toronto. In the spring. If I can find the fare.
I said I'd pay your fare, Nancy.
Rupert, I saw Brigadier Fenwick at the club. He says he doesn't remember you at Arnhem.
Fenwick doesn't remember his own wife, Locke.
Fenwick remembers everything. I had lunch with him on Tuesday.
You had lunch with Fenwick. Of course you did.
He paid, Rupert. That's how I knew he was serious.
What did the Brigadier have to say?
That the young men at the bridge were very brave. And that not one of them was called Ashcombe.
Fenwick was shot in the head in nineteen forty four. He's been forgetting things ever since.
He'd say it himself, Edith. He says it every November.
Rupert, you're shouting. The neighbours will think it's a party.
It is a party, darling. It's our anniversary. I'm entitled to shout.
Hobbs is very quiet tonight. Is he well?
Hobbs is always quiet. It's why I pay him.
Hobbs hears everything, don't you, Hobbs?
Max, you've been at Rupert's table, what, five years?
Six. Rupert feeds me and I keep his name out of the paper. It's a very English arrangement.
The wine is the expensive part, Rupert. My silence is a bargain.
Nancy, does Rupert really take heart pills?
Digitalis. One drop in water, every night. Doctor's orders.
I'm sixty eight, Max. My heart is an antique. Like the furniture.
The furniture is from Harrods, Rupert. I checked.
Where are you going this winter, Celia?
Rupert wants Scotland. I want Monte Carlo. We'll go to Scotland.
Monte Carlo is full of people like Max.
That's why it's so lovely, Rupert.
Max goes to Monte Carlo every winter. Don't you, Max?
Every winter. This winter I may not go alone.
I'm watching, Celia. Novelists watch. It's cheaper than going out.
Locke, will you come to Ashcombe at Christmas? Rupert wants to shoot something.
As long as it isn't me, Celia.
Pheasant, Locke. Only pheasant. I've never shot anything that could shoot back.
Now there's a quote for Monday.
Max, you collect quotes the way other men collect stamps.
Stamps don't pay, darling. Quotes do.
Hobbs, leave the wine. I'll fetch the twenty eight up myself.
Rupert, let Hobbs go. You'll miss the fish.
Nobody touches the twenty eight but me, Celia. Ten years tonight. It deserves the right hands.
Rupert chose the whole menu himself this year. Even the claret at the sorbet. I've never known him so interested.
Max, how did you find out about the medals? Your war hero.
A man in a pub in Brighton, Edith. He sold them. He remembered the buyer. Men always remember a buyer who pays cash.
And the buyer was somebody we know.
Rupert's father was the same about wine. He slept in the cellar all through the Blitz.
A sensible man. Cellars are very safe places.
The safest place in London, Locke. Nobody goes down there but me.
Hobbs carries the bottles up, Nancy. He doesn't choose them.
Excuse me, all of you. I won't be long.
He's very particular about that wine.
He's very particular about everything that's his.
Uncle Rupert's taking a long time with that wine.
The cellar is a long way down, and he stops to talk to every bottle.
There. The twenty eight. Decanted, and breathing. Hobbs will pour it at the sorbet.
At the sorbet? Isn't that unusual?
It's my anniversary, Edith. I'll drink claret with my custard if I want to.
Rupert, you'll have to tell me about this twenty eight. I know nothing about wine.
Nineteen twenty eight. A great year in Bordeaux. My father laid down two cases, and there are four bottles left.
Four bottles left, and you're opening one for Max. You must be very fond of him.
I'm fond of everybody tonight, Edith. It's my anniversary.
He's never been fond of me in his life, Inspector. That's what worries me.
Rupert, did you finish my proofs? You kept them a fortnight.
I read the last chapter twice, Edith. I wanted to be sure how it was done.
It was obvious. I told you.
Nancy, the hospital must keep a great deal of poison about.
Locked away, Inspector. Everything is signed for. Every drop.
Unlike a chemist in the country.
Ten years, Rupert. What's the secret?
Separate bedrooms and a good butler.
I'm not joking, darling. Hobbs is a very good butler.
Inspector, what was your strangest case?
A man in Putney who poisoned his wife with her own marmalade. Took him eleven years.
A spoonful at a time. She said it tasted a little sharp. She was very fond of marmalade.
Celia. The terrace, after dinner. I need some air.
What are you two whispering about?
Our friends in the middle are very quiet. Are you enjoying yourselves?
They're listening, Inspector. Clever people listen.
And on Monday, clever people read.
Celia, you've had your hair done. For anyone special?
Is that the sorbet coming? I can hear spoons.
Hobbs can hear a spoon from three floors away.
My old sergeant used to say, watch the man who's quiet at his own party.
No. He's talked about the war all evening.
People ask, Locke. A man can't help being asked.
Nobody asked tonight, darling. You told them anyway.
Uncle Rupert's medals are in a glass case in the hall. You walked past them on the way in.
I noticed them, Nancy. They're very clean.
Never been worn, you see. Not by him, anyway.
Lemon sorbet. To clean the palate before the beef. Very proper.
It's lovely. Like eating a cloud.
Rupert, you're not eating your sorbet.
I'm saving myself for the toast, darling.
Max, what are you writing in that little book?
Notes, Nancy. Monday doesn't write itself.
Put it away, Max. Not at my table.
As you like, Rupert. It's all up here anyway.
Glasses up, everybody. The twenty eight. To Max, and to Monday.
Rupert. That's not the twenty eight. That's... it's bitter... my throat...
Let me through, I'm a nurse!
Sit down, Nancy. Nobody move. Let me see him.
He can't be. He was talking. He was just talking.
Bitter almonds. On his lips, and in his glass. Cyanide.
Nobody touches that glass. And nobody leaves this table.
Locke, you can't seriously think that one of us...
I think one of you, Rupert. Very seriously.
Inspector, his eyes. Shouldn't somebody close his eyes?
Leave him exactly as he is, Nancy. He's the only one of us who can't lie.
He was laughing, Edith. A minute ago he was laughing at Rupert.
I'll telephone when I know who to tell them to collect.
We can't just sit here with him.
We can, Missus Vane. We will. Everybody stays exactly where they were when he drank.
You two, in the middle. You've been sitting there all evening with your ears open. Keep them open.
There's a board at the end of the table. Put your pin on whoever you think did this, and move it as often as these people change their stories.
When the pudding comes, the board closes.
This is absurd. A parlour game, with Max lying there.
Max would have loved it, Rupert. He'd have written it up.
He said the sorbet tasted bitter. No. He said the wine.
He said that's not the twenty eight. Remember that, all of you.
My captain says something very like that. In my book. Before he dies.
We'll come to your book, Missus Vane.
Locke, I must protest. My guests are not suspects. They're my guests.
Your guest is on the floor, Rupert. The rest of you are suspects.
I've never been a suspect before.
It's very bracing, Nancy. I've been one twice. Both times for a review.
Locke, you've known all of us for years. You can't think it's one of us.
I've known a great many murderers for years, Celia. Usually longer than they knew I knew.
I can't eat. I can't possibly eat.
Shall I hold the beef, sir?
No, Hobbs. Serve the beef. People talk more when they're eating.
Very good, sir. And for Mister Harrow?
Serve him too, Hobbs. He'd have hated to miss the beef.
Horseradish, please, Hobbs. Lots. It's been a trying evening.
Nancy. You left the table during the soup.
To fetch my bag from the terrace. I'm on call.
And was everything in your bag?
No. A vial is missing. Digitalis. I counted it twice when I came back in.
Digitalis. That's the heart medicine. That would do it, wouldn't it?
It would. Enough of it would stop a horse.
Rupert takes digitalis. Nancy brings it for him.
One drop in water, Edith. Not a vial in the claret.
And it doesn't smell of almonds, Inspector. Digitalis smells of nothing at all.
Who knew the bag was on the terrace?
Everybody. I put it down by the champagne when we came up.
Nancy, did you go anywhere else while you were out? The pantry? The cellar?
No. The terrace and back. You can ask Hobbs, he saw me on the terrace.
Hobbs. The twenty eight, at the toast. Who poured it?
I poured the table, sir. All but Mister Harrow's.
His lordship poured it himself, sir. In the pantry, during the fish. He handed me the glass and said Mister Harrow was to have the first of the bottle.
It's the host's privilege, Hobbs. The first glass for the guest of honour.
And you carried that glass to Max's place, Hobbs.
I did, sir. On the tray, by itself. Nobody else touched it.
And I found this under the coats in the hall, sir. A little brown bottle.
My digitalis! I must have dropped it on the way in.
Then that's one thing that didn't kill him.
I'm sorry, Inspector. I didn't even notice it was gone until I counted.
You counted, Nancy. That's more than most people do. Why did you count?
Habit. On the wards, if you lose a drop, you write a page.
You see, Locke? A full bottle. A careless girl. Nothing more.
I'm not careless, Uncle Rupert. I'm tired.
Tired and careless are the same thing after midnight, dear. Ask any publisher.
Death at the Captain's Table. Out in March. Heinemann.
Cyanide. In his glass. During a toast. Oh dear.
But everybody at this table knows the plot! I bore people with it constantly. I bored you with it in July.
And Rupert read the proofs. Rupert said the ending was obvious.
It was obvious, Edith. The butler did it.
Not tonight, my lord. I was polishing the spoons.
Where were you during the fish, Missus Vane?
Here. Eating it. With both hands, in front of everybody. Ask anyone.
Inspector, I write murders. I don't commit them. It would ruin the sales.
I'm told it does the opposite, Missus Vane.
And I'd never use the poison from my own book. It's terribly bad form.
Celia. When I checked Max, there were letters in his jacket.
Monday, my darling. We'll tell him on Monday. Your hand, I think.
Yes. All right. Yes. Max and I. Since the spring.
You knew, darling. You always know everything. You just never say.
I knew about the letters, Celia. I didn't know about Monday.
Well. That's a motive. For both of you.
I loved him, Edith. You don't poison a man you're about to run away with.
Unless he's changed his mind, Celia.
He hadn't. He said so on the terrace. Before dinner.
You sat beside him all evening.
I sat beside our friend here, Inspector. With our friend between us. I couldn't have reached his glass without climbing over them.
That's true. I watched. I always watch Celia when Max is talking.
Rupert. You said you knew about the letters. How long?
Since August. Celia leaves things in her coat pockets. She always has.
And you said nothing. For two months.
What would I say, darling? I'm sixty eight, and he made you laugh.
Aunt Celia, were you really going to leave?
On Tuesday. We had tickets for Nice. Max said Monday would pay for everything.
Monday seems to have paid for a great deal.
Thank you, Hobbs. At least something tonight is still civilised.
One more thing from Max's jacket. His notebook. Monday's column.
R.A. Never at Arnhem. Spent the war in a supply office in Aldershot. The medals were bought at auction in Brighton.
Or Ronald Archer. Or Roger Ames. Half my club are R.A., Locke.
Your club is a very decorated place, Rupert.
The blossom, Rupert. You said the blossom was out on the trees at Arnhem.
One misremembers, Edith. It was forty years ago.
Forty years is a long time to remember a battle you weren't at.
I've known you thirty years, Locke. You think I would poison a man at my own table, on my own anniversary?
Rupert went down to the cellar during the fish.
For the claret! Which you all drank!
We drank ours, Rupert. Max drank his.
But where would anybody get cyanide? In London?
Ashcombe. The wasps. Jenkins puts it down every August.
Jenkins has the key to the shed, not me.
There's a key on your watch chain, darling. There always has been.
This is a very good Stilton. I don't know how I can taste it, but I can.
Grief makes some people hungry, Edith. We see it on the wards.
Then I must be grieving terribly.
Hobbs. When his lordship came up from the cellar, which way did he come?
By the pantry, sir. Up the back stairs, the way the bottles come.
And was he alone in the pantry?
Quite alone, sir. He sent me up to the table ahead of him.
He kept us waiting twenty minutes.
Twenty two. I timed him. I time everything. It's how I plot.
Twenty two minutes to bring up one bottle.
And a decanter, Locke. And I had to find the funnel.
You said you'd decanted it. You said it was breathing.
It was breathing, Nancy. Somebody in this room should be.
Inspector, I've just realised. I'll have to rewrite my ending. Everyone at this table knows it now.
Change the poison, Missus Vane. Nobody ever checks.
A wife with a lover. A niece with a missing bottle. A novelist with a plot. A butler with a glass. And a host with a war he never fought.
I didn't fight it either, sir.
No, Hobbs. But you never said you did.
You two in the middle. The board. You have until the pudding.
Rupert. Look at me. Did you?
So do I, darling. So do I.
When the pudding comes, I'm going to have a very large glass of something. Not the twenty eight.
Inspector, this is my house. You can't keep us at this table all night.
Only until the pudding, Rupert. Then you can all go wherever I tell you.
Max would have loved this. All of us, frightened of a pudding.
In my books the detective always waits for the last course. It's very cruel.
It's very effective, Missus Vane. Nobody ever leaves before the pudding.
Locke, if it was Rupert. What happens to him?
The same as anybody, Celia. A cell, a judge, and a great many reporters. Max would have hated to miss it.
There'll be a trial? I've always wanted to attend a trial. Properly. With a sandwich.
Because if I stop talking, dear, I'll start crying. And I never cry before the pudding.
You haven't said it was me, Locke.
No, Rupert. I haven't said anything yet.
The pudding is coming up now, sir.
The pudding, my lord. Chocolate torte.
Pudding. Pins down, please. The board is closed.
Max was not poisoned at this table. I watched him all evening. Nobody reached across him. Not even Celia.
The claret was poured for the table from one decanter, and we all drank it, and we are all still here. So it was in one glass.
Nancy's digitalis is full. Missus Vane never left her fish. Hobbs carried a glass that somebody else poured.
And Celia had every reason to keep Max alive until Monday.

But somebody went down alone during the fish, and poured one glass himself, in the pantry. Somebody with cyanide in a shed and the key on his watch chain. Somebody who remembers blossom at a battle in September.
Forty years of being a hero at dinner. Forty years of the bridge, and the blossom, and the noise. They believed every word.
And on Monday, a man I had fed at this table for six years was going to sell me to the newspapers for a paragraph. And run off with my wife on the money.
I took Edith's ending, Edith. You were right. It wasn't obvious at all.
Rupert Ashcombe, I am arresting you for the murder of Max Harrow.
Let me pay Hobbs first, Locke. He's owed for March.
And then telephone the station, Hobbs. Ask for Inspector Dawes. Tell him Locke has one for him.
Ten years. Ten years, and I never knew if a single thing you told me was true.
The cellar was true, Celia. And the view. And you. You were always true.
You held my hand at Mummy's funeral. You told me about the bridge. You said being brave was just being frightened for a bit longer than everyone else.
That was true too, Nancy. I just wasn't the one who said it first. A man called Fenwick said it to me in nineteen forty four. In Aldershot.
I don't want to know any more.
I gave him the idea. My ending. He read it in my proofs and he did it.
He'd have done it with a carving knife if you'd written a carving knife, Missus Vane. You gave him a recipe. He brought the appetite.
That's very kind, Inspector. It's also very good. May I use it?
Locke. I'd like to wait somewhere else. Not across the table from him.
The library, Rupert. Hobbs will lock the door when he's back. You know the way.
I know the way. I'm not going to run, Locke. Where would I run? Every man at my club knows my face.
Don't be kind to me, Edith. I'll fall to pieces, and there's still the torte.
Then I shall be beastly. You look dreadful in green.
Thank you, Edith. That's much better.
When he said blossom, Nancy. Nobody who was at Arnhem talks about the blossom. They talk about the noise, and they don't talk about it at dinner.
Max always knew. Knowing was his job. Being careful wasn't.
Inspector Dawes is on his way, sir. Ten minutes. He asked me to say thank you, and to say that it's your round.
Thank you, Hobbs. Lock the library door, would you? His lordship is waiting in there.
Very good, sir. He asked for a brandy on the way past. I took the liberty of giving him the twenty eight.
The last bottle of it, my lady. I thought he ought to have it before the police did.
Inspector, our two friends in the middle. They've been very good. They haven't said a word all night.
They didn't need to, Missus Vane. They were watching. Some of them had their pins on him before the beef.
Clever people listen. I said so at the sole.
I had mine on Edith. I'm so sorry, Edith.
Don't be, dear. I'd have had mine on me too. I'm very suspicious.
What do I tell people, Locke? Tomorrow. At the club, at church. In the papers.
Tell them the truth, Celia. It'll be in the papers either way, and the truth is better written.
Max would have written it on Monday. And it would have been very good, and very unkind.
It would. He'd have called me the green widow.
Aunt Celia, come and stay with me. I've got a sofa, and a kettle, and nobody ever comes round.
That's the nicest thing anybody's said to me all night, darling.
You can have the sofa. I'm never home anyway. I'm always on call.
He stays exactly where he is until Dawes has seen him. Then they'll take him down in the lift. Quietly.
He'd hate quietly. He'd want a band.
He can have one at the funeral, Missus Vane. I'll see to it.
Will you take the torte, my lady? Cook made it for the anniversary.
Leave it, Hobbs. I'll have it in the morning, for breakfast, in bed, and I'll cry into it.
Inspector, Max's notebook. What will happen to it?
Evidence, Nancy. Every page of it. Half of London will be very glad it's locked up.
And the other half will be furious they weren't in it.
Locke. Thank you. I don't think I could have borne it if it had been somebody I liked.
I know, Celia. That's why I watched him all evening and not you.
Inspector, will you write this one up? For the memoirs?
Chapter four, Missus Vane. The claret. I think it'll be shorter than the vicar.
Make me cleverer than I was. Everybody else will.
You were clever enough. You timed him. Twenty two minutes. It'll be in the evidence.
Then I've been useful. How mortifying.
Aunt Celia, Toronto. Max said he'd lend me the fare on Monday. I suppose that's gone too.
Nothing's gone, darling. Max left his money to me, and I'm going to spend it on you. He'd have liked that. It would have annoyed Rupert terribly.
Thank you. I'll send you blossom. Real blossom, in the spring.
Send me a postcard, Nancy. I've had enough blossom for one lifetime.
The police are in the lift, sir. I'll go down and meet them, if I may.
Do, Hobbs. And thank you. You were very good tonight.
Ten years, sir. I'm owed a pound by Missus Vane on the marriage. I don't suppose I'll collect it now.
You'll collect it, Hobbs. With interest. It lasted the ten years. It just didn't last the eleventh.
Inspector, will you be all right? Going home tonight? On your own?
I've a cat called Sergeant, Nancy, and a bottle of something that isn't the twenty eight. We'll manage.
Come to us for Christmas, Locke. You and Sergeant. Me and Nancy.
Monte Carlo, Locke. I've had enough of Scotland. I've had enough of everything Rupert wanted.
Aunt Celia, the flat. Will you keep it?
The view, darling. I'll keep the view. Rupert always said it cost more than the furniture. He was right about one thing.
And I'll still be downstairs. Reading in the bath. Every Monday.
There won't be a column on Monday, Edith.
Then I'll read the old ones. Out loud. He'd like that.
Downstairs, all of you. The Rovers. Dawes will want us together, and I want a drink that nobody here has poured.
A large one. In a glass I've watched the whole way.
Come with us. Please. I don't want to be the only one at the bar who knew him.
